data.name: Vishwamaya
data.gender_notes: Vishwamaya is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from Sanskrit words 'Vishwa' (universe) and 'maya' (illusion). The name Vishwamaya carries the meaning “Universe's Illusion” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Vishwamaya usually hope their child will grow to embody universe's illusion and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the divine power of creation and manifestation.
data.etymology: Vishwamaya belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Universe's Illusion.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Vishwamaya total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Vishwamaya holds a significant cultural impact in Hinduism, as it refers to one who has the intelligence and wisdom to understand and perceive the intricacies of the universe, and is therefore considered a highly knowledgeable and enlightened individual.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Vishwamaya represents the divine power of understanding and perceiving the true nature of reality, which is often described as an illusion or 'maya' in Hindu texts. It denotes a seeker who has transcended the mundane understanding of the world and is able to comprehend the deeper, inner workings of the universe.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Vishwamaya: One who embodies universal wisdom and understanding. Embraces the infinite knowledge of the universe within oneself.

vedic_reference.note: Not found in Vedas or Upanishads

historical_references.reference: The sage Vishwamitra, also known as Vishwamitra Maharshi, was a legendary sage and a great Rishi in Hinduism. He is believed to have lived during Treta Yuga, around 3000 BCE. The name Vishwamitra means 'all-knowing' or 'omniscient'. He was a celebrated sage who performed rigorous Tapasya (penance) to obtain the divine boon of bringing the Devas and Asuras together.
historical_references.context: Legendary sage and Rishi who performed intense penance to bring the Devas and Asuras together

historical_references.reference: Another reference to the name Vishwamaya is found in the Mahabharata where it is mentioned that the great warrior Bhishma, during his final moments before his death, attained the knowledge of the entire universe (Vishwam) by the grace of the sage Vishwamitra, who was called Vishwamaya or the 'all-wise'. This event is believed to have occurred during the Mahabharata war which took place around 3067 BCE and 3045 BCE.
historical_references.time_period: Mahabharata war, around 3067 BCE and 3045 BCE
historical_references.context: Great sage who imparted the knowledge of the entire universe to Bhishma during his final moments

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's interconnected world, the name Vishwamaya continues to be cherished by Hindu families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Hindu name websites where expectant parents research meaningful names. The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.

name_in_real_life.story: Priya Vishwamaya, a teacher in Bali, Indonesia, shares that their name Vishwamaya meaning "Universe's Illusion" has been a constant source of inspiration, motivating them to follow Hindu values and serve their community.
